children: By George Glover, Kit Norton, and Mariapaula Gonzalez

Stocks struggled to rally Friday as Marvell Technology's disappointing earnings report and Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole warning that cooling inflation hasn't done enough to relieve consumers weighed on market sentiment.

Marvell Technology fell 10%. The chips and networking company's second-quarter earnings beat analysts' expectations, but not by enough to wow investors following a strong run for shares, which were up 184% for the year through Thursday's close. A chunk of revenue from the warrant deal with Alphabet-owned Google also was already embedded in Marvell's guidance.
Nvidia dropped 4.6% after ending the previous session up 8.7%. Intel and Lumentum also declined along with Marvell.

PayPal fell 12.7%. The financial-technology company Stripe and private-equity firm Advent International have given up on acquiring PayPal, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Stripe and Advent declined to comment. PayPal didn't respond to a request for comment.

Workday rose 5.8% after the enterprise software company posted better-than-expected second-quarter earnings and raised its guidance. There is also speculation that private equity firm Silver Lake has held talks to acquire Workday, though no such deal has been announced.
Other best-performing stocks in the S&P 500 included Domino's Pizza, ServiceNow Inc., and Lululemon Athletica.
Elastic rose 19% after the software company topped analysts' first-quarter earnings targets and raised its guidance.

Solstice Advanced Materials gained 13% after the company called off the acquisition of Element Solutions that would have turned the company into even more of an artificial-intelligence play. Investors wanted both companies to remain separate.
Gap advanced 13% after the retailer reported a second-quarter earnings beat and named a new CEO for Old Navy.

Affirm rose 0.4%. The financial technology company comfortably beat Wall Street's quarterly estimates. Gross merchandise volume, a measure of all transactions processed on Affirm's platform within a specific period, jumped 36% to $14.1 billion.

Iren dropped nearly 13%. The emerging so-called neocloud late Thursday posted adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, or Ebitda, well below Wall Street's expectations. Total revenue, however, came in above expectations for its fiscal fourth quarter ended June 30. Revenue from AI cloud services grew 110% sequentially to $70.5 million.
A new quantum stock has begun trading. Shares of Pasqal, a French developer of neutral atom quantum computers, soared 95% on Friday in their U.S. market debut.

Rubrik fell 13% after the cloud data security company reported better-than-expected quarterly earnings. Rubrik also posted subscription annual recurring revenue growth of 33% and raised its fiscal-year profit and revenue outlook.
Autodesk declined 3.7% after the software developer's outlook fell short of expectations, overshadowing a second-quarter earnings beat.
